quiz.0.question: What is Verdicchio's ageing potential?
quiz.0.options.1: 10–15 years or more for top producers
quiz.0.explanation: Top-quality Verdicchio (especially Matelica DOCG Riserva) can age 10–20 years, developing extraordinary complexity — comparable to white Burgundy.
quiz.1.question: What is the primary variety of Vino Nobile di Montepulciano DOCG?
quiz.1.options.1: Prugnolo Gentile (a clone of Sangiovese) — minimum 70%
quiz.1.explanation: Despite its name, Vino Nobile di Montepulciano uses Prugnolo Gentile (a Sangiovese clone, minimum 70%) — not the 'Montepulciano' grape variety. This is one of Italian wine's most persistent confusions.
quiz.2.question: Why does Sagrantino have the world's highest tannin content?
quiz.2.options.0: The wine is always aged for very long periods
quiz.2.options.1: The grape has uniquely high concentrations of proanthocyanidins (condensed tannins) in its thick skins
quiz.2.options.2: Winemakers add tannin powder during production
quiz.2.options.3: It is always fermented with stems
quiz.2.explanation: Sagrantino's extraordinarily thick skins contain an exceptionally high concentration of proanthocyanidins (condensed tannins) — a genetic characteristic unique to this variety.
quiz.3.question: Why is Pecorino grape called Pecorino?
quiz.3.options.1: Sheep (pecora) used to graze on the grapes during harvest, and shepherds also brought the vines across regions
quiz.3.options.2: It was discovered by a cheesemaker
quiz.3.options.3: Its leaves look like sheep's wool
quiz.3.explanation: Pecorino grape gets its name from sheep (pecora in Italian) — the animals used to eat the ripe, sweet grapes. Migratory shepherds also helped spread the vine across central Italy.
